Weight Interpretation

column6: Companies with faster growth drive 40% more revenue from personalization; good ICP is the foundation for segmentation/personalization.
column7: Companies that grow faster drive 40 percent more of their revenue from personalization.
column8: McKinsey — The value of getting personalization right
column11: Keep high. Source is credible but indirect: ICP enables segmentation/personalization, not an ICP-specific win-rate study.
column13: Need one ICP-specific source if possible; current evidence supports segmentation importance.

column6: Salesforce reports reps only spend 30% of their week selling, so poor-fit leads waste scarce selling capacity.
column7: Reps only spend 30% of their time selling during an average week.
column11: Keep high. Lead quality has direct productivity impact because sellers have limited actual selling time.
column13: Good support for prioritization/qualification, but pair with CRM data if available.

column6: McKinsey finds personalization can reduce CAC by up to 50%, lift revenue 5–15%, and improve marketing ROI 10–30%.
column7: Reduce customer acquisition costs by as much as 50 percent, lift revenues by 5 to 15 percent.
column11: Keep or slightly raise. Clear messaging/positioning supports personalized buying journeys and stronger acquisition economics.
column13: Strong numeric GTM evidence, though not only positioning.

column6: CMI/B2B benchmark takeaway reports 56% struggle with ROI attribution/tracking journeys and top performers link success to audience understanding.
column7: 56% of B2B marketers struggle to attribute ROI / track customer journeys.
column8: Content Marketing Institute / MX Group — B2B Benchmarks Takeaway
column11: Raise slightly. Channel strategy matters when teams can connect channels to pipeline and customer journeys.
column13: Good for channel measurement; find source on channel ROI by mix if time.

column6: CMI/B2B benchmark says 56% struggle to attribute ROI or track customer journeys, making attribution a measurable GTM gap.
column7: 56% struggle to attribute ROI / track customer journeys.
column8: Content Marketing Institute / MX Group — B2B Benchmarks Takeaway
column11: Keep high. Attribution directly affects budget allocation, pipeline forecasting, and knowing which channels work.
column13: Credible benchmark; would be stronger with pipeline-attribution study.

column6: Only 22% of B2B marketers rate content marketing as extremely/very successful; success is tied to audience understanding, quality, and aligned goals.
column7: Only 22% of B2B marketers rate content marketing as extremely/very successful.
column8: Content Marketing Institute / MX Group — B2B Benchmarks Takeaway
column11: Keep at 1.00 unless cadence is pipeline-tied. Cadence alone matters less than quality, goals, and attribution.
column13: Evidence supports execution discipline, not volume for its own sake.

column6: HBR/MIT research found firms contacting leads within an hour were nearly 7x more likely to qualify than firms waiting longer.
column7: Firms that contacted potential customers within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify the lead.
column8: Harvard Business Review — The Short Life of Online Sales Leads
column11: Raise. This is one of the strongest direct conversion findings; speed-to-lead should be heavily weighted.
column13: Very strong numeric evidence; source is older but widely cited and directly relevant.

column6: Salesforce reports reps only spend 30% of their week selling; qualification protects limited seller time by filtering poor-fit opportunities.
column7: Reps only spend 30% of their time selling during an average week.
column11: Keep high or raise slightly. Structured qualification affects efficiency and forecast quality.
column13: Could use win-rate-by-qualification source if found.

column6: Salesforce emphasizes forecasting accuracy and pipeline visibility as key sales operations needs; poor CRM hygiene damages forecast reliability.
column7: Sales reps spend almost one full day of their workweek on prospecting.
column11: Keep medium-high. Pipeline integrity is operationally important, but source is less directly numeric than SLA/CRO.
column13: Need internal CRM/session data to validate.

column6: Forrester/SiriusDecisions highlights buyer/customer experience as a major decision driver; objection handling is part of consistent buying experience.
column7: Customer experience can make or break your success.
column11: Keep at 1.00. Important but evidence is less direct and more qualitative than lead speed or win/loss analysis.
column13: Use as supporting evidence, not a main weight driver.

column6: Gartner-referenced summary says rigorous win/loss programs have seen 15–30% revenue increases and up to 50% win-rate improvement.
column7: 15% to 30% increase in revenue and up to 50% improvement in win rates.
column8: Clozd summary of Gartner win/loss research
column11: Raise. This is strong conversion-learning evidence if accepted as a Gartner-derived source.
column13: Secondary source summarizing Gartner; good, but original Gartner may be paywalled.

column6: Baymard benchmark says average large ecommerce site can gain 35.26% conversion-rate improvement through better checkout design.
column7: The average large-sized ecommerce site can gain a 35.26% increase in conversion rate.
column8: Baymard Institute — Cart & checkout abandonment statistics
column11: Raise. Direct conversion lift evidence; CRO testing should not be weighted as low as 1.00 for digital funnels.
column13: Strong for ecommerce/digital; weight may vary by business type.

column6: Amplitude benchmark: top products retain 18.5% of users at 3 months vs 3.8% median; gap starts with faster value delivery.
column7: Top products retain 18.5% of users while median products retain just 3.8%.
column8: Amplitude — Time to Value Drives User Retention
column11: Keep high or raise. Time-to-value is directly tied to retention and customer activation.

column6: OnRamp report says 48% abandon onboarding if they do not see value quickly; 65% using digital onboarding reduced TTV by at least 25%.
column7: 48% of customers abandon onboarding if they do not see value quickly.
column11: Raise slightly. Onboarding is the mechanism that delivers early value and reduces early churn risk.
column13: Good source; verify full report if available.

column6: Gainsight defines health scores as combined usage, engagement, support, and satisfaction signals to detect renewal risk early.
column7: Customer health scores help teams identify risk before renewal.
column11: Keep high but mark evidence as operational, not causal. Health scoring enables proactive risk detection.
column13: Needs stronger numeric validation; source is credible in CS but vendor-based.

column6: Gainsight churn benchmark: mid-market SaaS commonly sees 5–8% annual churn; early-stage startups may see 10–15%.
column7: Mid-market SaaS companies often report annual churn rates of 5–8%.
column11: Raise. Retention is directly tied to revenue durability, expansion, and customer success health.
column13: Very important category outcome; also use company-specific churn if available.

column6: Gainsight frames QBRs as quarterly strategic meetings focused on ROI, alignment, retention, and expansion, but numeric lift evidence is weaker.
column7: QBRs are strategic meetings focused on ROI, alignment, retention, and expansion.
column11: Keep or slightly raise only if enterprise/high-touch. QBR impact depends on customer segment and ACV.
column13: Weak numeric evidence; good qualitative support.

column6: Nielsen global survey: 92% trust recommendations from friends/family above all other advertising forms; advocacy supports referral-led demand.
column7: 92 percent of consumers around the world say they trust earned media.
column11: Keep at 1.00 or 1.05. Advocacy is valuable but usually downstream after retention and onboarding are working.
column13: Good trust statistic; B2B-specific referral evidence would improve this row.
